evidence: Token1 box: 'token1 / sampled by prefill'; token2: 'first decode output'; token3: 'second decode output'. All feed 'append K/V per layer-head'. Caption: 'written when that token is next processed as input, one step after it is sampled.'

issue: Secondary labels are set in small, low-contrast gray type below the 8 pt print floor: 'sampled by prefill', 'first decode output', 'second decode output', 'store K', 'store V', 'read V', 'read K'.

issue: The smallest in-figure annotations (e.g. 'sampled by prefill', 'first decode output', 'h1–h4' in Fig 1.1; 'BPE splits corpus-driven', 'one vec/token', 'per layer × head' in Fig 1.2) render noticeably smaller than the 8pt body/caption text at 150 dpi and may fall under the stated 8pt print floor for figure in-text annotations. issue: The figure depicts each token's K/V being appended on the SAME step the token is sampled, contradicting the figure's own caption and the book's prose. This is the single most consequential semantic detail in the chapter (it is what makes the KV cache a cache rather than a recomputation), and the drawing gets it backwards.
evidence: Caption: 'every token adds one K/V per layer per head — written when that token is next processed as an input, one step after it is sampled.' Drawing: token1 ('sampled from prefill'), token2 ('first decode output'), token3 ('second decode output') each have a direct arrow into the 'append K/V per layer-head' box, i.e. the sampled token's own K/V is appended at the step it is sampled. Prose on printed p.14 (PDF p.34) states the opposite explicitly: 'the sampled next token is the output of this step and the input of the following step, whose forward pass then computes and appends its K/V. A token's K/V therefore enters the cache on the step in which it is the input, not on the step in which it is sampled.'
root_cause: The figure was drawn as a token-to-cache accumulation story rather than as a step-indexed story, so the one-step lag that the caption and prose emphasize is not encoded.
correction: Re-index the figure by step: show 'step t: input token_{i-1} -> compute K/V -> append K/V for token_{i-1}' and 'step t+1: input token_i -> ...', with the sampled token_i shown as the OUTPUT of step t and the INPUT of step t+1. At minimum, add a one-step offset between the token column and the append box (e.g. a bracket labelled 'appended on the NEXT step') and change the token sub-labels to 'sampled at step t' / 'appended at step t+1'.
acceptance_test: Tracing only the arrows, a reader concludes that a token's K/V is written on the step in which that token is the input, not on the step in which it is sampled; the figure and the printed p.14 prose agree without needing the caption to arbitrate.

issue: An unlabeled connector runs from the top of the token column across the top of the figure and drops into the top of the 'append K/V per layer-head' box. Its origin and meaning are not stated anywhere, and it duplicates the side connector from the same token column into the same box, so the reader cannot tell whether it is a feedback path, a second input, or a stray artifact.
evidence: Rendered geometry: a horizontal line at y~160 from x~130 to x~250, then a downward arrowhead into the top edge of the orange 'append K/V' box at x~250, y~180. The token column boxes sit at x~95-165 with their tops at y~185, so the line appears to originate just above token1. Separately, each token box has a short horizontal arrow into the left edge of the orange box.
root_cause: A connector was added (probably intended as the 'read for attention -> next token' feedback) but was left unlabelled and unanchored.
correction: Either delete the top connector, or give it a definite meaning and label it. If it is meant to express the loop (cache read -> next token -> next step), route it from the 'read for attention' box back to the token column and label it 'next step's input', which would also make the one-step lag of FIG-1.1-A visible.
acceptance_test: Every connector in the figure has a label or an unambiguous source and destination; no two connectors connect the same pair of elements with different implied meanings.

issue: The 'read K' connector is routed around the outside right edge of the 'stored V — values' box with only ~0.07 in of clearance, and it enters the 'read for attention' box from the right while 'read V' enters from the top. The asymmetric entry and the hugging route make it easy to misread the green path as belonging to the stored-V box.
evidence: Rendered geometry: the green line runs vertically at x~470, immediately right of the stored-V box whose right edge is at x~460 (10 px at 150 dpi ~ 0.07 in), from the bottom of the 'stored K' box down to y~440, then turns left into the right edge of the 'read for attention' box. The 'read V' arrow is a short vertical drop from the stored-V box into the top of the read box, with its label at x~355-385, y~400. The 'read K' label sits at x~430-460, y~395-405, i.e. beside the stored-V box rather than beside its own arrow.
root_cause: The two read paths were laid out independently and the K path was pushed outside the box column to avoid overlapping the V path, without re-checking label placement.
correction: Give the K and V read paths symmetric treatment: e.g. both drop from their respective boxes into the top of the 'read for attention' box, with 'read K' and 'read V' labels directly above their own arrows; or merge them into a single labelled 'read K and V' connector. Increase clearance to at least 0.15 in from any box edge.
acceptance_test: Each of 'read K' and 'read V' is positioned immediately above the arrow it names, and no connector passes within 0.1 in of an unrelated box.

issue: Caption is a single run-on sentence with a comma splice, and it describes per-head enumeration that the figure does not show.
evidence: Caption: 'This is a single-layer detail view: one layer's stored K and stored V drawn separately, each enumerated per head (h1-hn), the full token-travel pipeline is in Fig 1.2 and the end-to-end pipeline in Fig 2.1, where the cache persists across the whole loop.' The figure shows one box per (K, V) labelled 'layer L . h1-hn' — a range label, not per-head enumeration.
root_cause: Caption written as one continuous sentence and not reconciled with the drawn content.
correction: Split the caption into two sentences, and either draw the per-head enumeration (a small stack of head slices) or reword to 'labelled by layer and head range (h1-hn)'.
acceptance_test: The caption contains no comma splice, and every element it attributes to the figure is visibly present in the figure.

issue: The read box is labelled 'read for attention / next token (i)'; the index (i) is never defined on the page, in the caption, or (as far as this page shows) anywhere in the surrounding text, so it reads as a stray symbol.
evidence: Rendered label: 'read for attention' with sub-label 'next token (i)'. The caption and the adjacent prose use 'the next token' with no index.
root_cause: Index notation carried over from a working draft without being introduced.
correction: Either drop '(i)' or introduce it in the caption ('the next token, index i, is the token whose K/V is being written').
acceptance_test: Every symbol appearing in a figure label is defined in the caption or the adjacent prose.

issue: Sub-annotation type in the token column ('sampled from prefill', 'first decode output', 'second decode output', 'adds one K/V') and in the stored-K/V boxes ('layer L . h1-hn') appears to fall below the 8 pt figure-annotation floor, and the last token box's sub-label ('adds one K/V') is an action rather than a provenance, unlike the other three.

root_cause: Annotation type size was not verified against the book's stated floor; the token column was filled with whatever text fit.
correction: Raise sub-annotation type to >= 8 pt at print size (widening the token column if needed) and make the fourth box's sub-label parallel in kind ('nth decode output' or 'adds one K/V at step n+1').
acceptance_test: All figure annotations measure >= 8 pt at print size; the four token sub-labels are grammatically parallel.

issue: The Token IDs box says 'integers order = position', which conflates token identity with positional encoding. Token IDs are vocabulary indices; position IDs are assigned separately and encoded by the model.
evidence: Label in the Token IDs box: 'integers / order = position'. The caption says 'text → tokenizer → IDs → embedding → attention' and does not mention position IDs. A reader can infer that the integer token ID encodes its position.
acceptance_test: Replace the label with 'integers; sequence order preserved' and add a separate 'position IDs' annotation on the path to the transformer/attention, or explicitly state that positions are assigned separately. Verify no arrow or label implies token ID = position.

issue: The arrow from Embedding to Attention is labeled 'attend', and the Attention box says 'computes Q, K, V for this token vs all past tokens'. This conflates the projection that produces Q/K/V with the attention operation and can imply that the embedding itself attends or that K/V for past tokens are recomputed.
evidence: Arrow label 'attend' between 'Embedding' and 'Attention'; Attention box text 'computes Q, K, V for this token vs all past tokens'; KV Cache box says 'read + write per layer × head' and the return arrow is labeled 'read past K,V'.
acceptance_test: Relabel the Embedding→Attention arrow 'project Q/K/V' or 'hidden state'; change the Attention box to 'Q from this token; attend over cached past K/V' (or equivalent). Keep 'attend' only for the attention operation, not the embedding transition.

issue: The figure draws a single 'Attention' box, which is precisely the misreading the caption warns against ('The K/V are produced within every applicable layer (not after a single "attention" stage)'). The caption's disclaimer cannot rescue a diagram whose visual grammar says 'one attention stage'.
evidence: Figure: 'Embedding -> attend -> Attention (compute Q,K,V for this vs all past tokens) -> append K,V -> KV Cache (read + write per layer + head)'. Caption: 'The K/V are produced within every applicable layer (not after a single "attention" stage)'. The only cue that layers exist is the small 'per layer + head' sub-label inside the KV Cache box.
root_cause: The figure was simplified to a linear token journey, and the layer dimension was relegated to a caption caveat instead of being encoded.
correction: Encode the layer dimension in the drawing: e.g. a stack of L blocks labelled 'Transformer block x L (attention + MLP)' with the KV Cache box labelled 'per layer x per head', or a brace marked 'x L layers' spanning the attention stage. Then shorten the caption caveat accordingly.
acceptance_test: A reader who sees only the figure can state that attention (and K/V production) happens once per layer, not once per token.

issue: Type inside the boxes is cramped and appears below the 8 pt figure-annotation floor: the Attention box's sub-label 'compute Q,K,V for this vs all past tokens' wraps to two lines that nearly fill the box, and the sub-labels throughout ('user prompt', 'characters', 'BPE splits', 'corpus-driven', 'ordered integers', 'ID to d-dim vector', 'one vec/token', 'read + write per layer + head') are set noticeably smaller than the box titles.
evidence: In the 150 dpi render (580 px for 8.5 in = 68 px/in) the sub-label glyph height is ~4-5 px, i.e. roughly 6-7 pt at print size, versus ~8-9 px (~11-12 pt) for the box titles. The Attention box (x~255-340, y~340-380) contains two lines of sub-label with ~3 px clearance top and bottom.
root_cause: Boxes were sized to fit the diagram rather than the type, and the annotation type size was not checked against the book's figure-annotation floor.
correction: Enlarge the sub-label type to the figure-annotation floor (>= 8 pt at print size) and widen/heighten the affected boxes (Attention, KV Cache, Embedding) to accommodate it without wrapping into the box border; shorten the strings if necessary ('compute Q,K,V (this + past)').
acceptance_test: At 100% print size on US Letter, every figure annotation is >= 8 pt and no text touches a box border.

issue: The caption refers to 'the backward arrow from the KV cache back to attention', but that arrow is drawn as a routed return path below the boxes, not as a backward arrow; and the caption's 'Color is figure-local decoration' disclaimer is not carried by Figs. 1.1 and 2.1, which also rely on color to distinguish read from write and to identify the initialize path.
evidence: Caption: 'the KV cache is a persistent state — written (append) and read (attend, the backward arrow from the KV cache back to attention) across steps — not a processing stage.' In the figure the green 'read past K,V' arrow leaves the bottom of the KV Cache box, runs left below the Attention box, and turns up into the Attention box's bottom edge. Figs. 1.1 and 2.1 have no color disclaimer.
root_cause: Caption written against an earlier draft of the layout; the disclaimer was added to one caption only.
correction: Describe the arrow by its label ('the green/grey arrow labelled read past K,V') rather than by direction, and add the same color disclaimer to Figs. 1.1 and 2.1 (or make the palette global and drop the disclaimer everywhere).
acceptance_test: Every caption's description of an arrow matches the arrow's drawn geometry and label, and the color convention is stated wherever color carries meaning.

issue: The 'read' path from the persistent KV cache to the decode transformer is drawn as a plain vertical line without a visible arrowhead, while the 'append' path has a clear upward arrowhead. The direction of the read path is therefore ambiguous.
evidence: Between 'PERSISTENT KV CACHE' and the DECODE transformer: left vertical line labeled 'read' has no visible arrowhead; right vertical line labeled 'append' has an upward arrowhead. Caption: 'each step reads the cached K/V, appends the new K/V'.
acceptance_test: Add a downward arrowhead to the 'read' path and make the read/append pair visually symmetric; verify the direction is unambiguous without relying on the caption.

issue: Several figure annotations are below the 8 pt print floor and low contrast: 'populate', 'read', 'append', 'initialize', 'loop', and 'conceptual per-step, per-layer cache I/O'.

figure: FIGURE 2.1 — The canonical end-to-end inference pipeline
issue: The green 'initialize' arrow terminates at the RIGHT end of the DECODE band, directly above the 'next token' box, instead of at the 'previous token' box at the LEFT end. As drawn, the first sampled token appears to initialize the next-token output rather than to become the decode loop's input.
evidence: In the render the green path leaves the right edge of 'first token' (x~450, y~175), runs right to x~467, drops to y~340, and turns left with an arrowhead at x~452 — inside the DECODE band, immediately above the 'next token' box (x 415-460, y 365-385). The 'previous token' box is at the far left (x~85-155). The caption states the opposite intent: 'The green initialize path seeds the loop with the first sampled token.' The 'loop' arrow already carries next token -> previous token along the bottom, so the drawn initialize path is redundant with, and visually contradicts, the loop.
root_cause: The initialize path was routed around the right margin to avoid crossing the KV-cache arrows, without checking that its endpoint lands on the box it is supposed to feed.
correction: Terminate the initialize arrow on the 'previous token' box (e.g. drop it down the left margin, or route it above the DECODE band and down into 'previous token'), and label the arrow 'first token becomes the decode input'. Alternatively, if the intent is that the first token enters the loop at the point where 'next token' is produced, redraw the loop so the sampled token is visibly re-injected at 'previous token' and drop the separate initialize arrow.
acceptance_test: Tracing only the arrows (ignoring the caption), a reader concludes that the first sampled token becomes the input of the first decode step, and no arrow terminates on the 'next token' box from outside the loop.

figure: FIGURE 2.1 — The canonical end-to-end inference pipeline
issue: The caption identifies a path by color ('The green initialize path'), which is meaningless in grayscale and in color-vision-deficient printing; and the book's color semantics are inconsistent across the three figures in this batch (green = 'read for attention' in Fig. 1.1, green = tokenizer/embedding in Fig. 1.2, green = 'initialize' in Fig. 2.1; orange = 'append K/V' in Fig. 1.1 but 'Token IDs' in Fig. 1.2).
evidence: Fig. 2.1 caption: 'The green initialize path seeds the loop with the first sampled token.' Fig. 1.1 uses green for the 'read for attention' box and the read arrows, orange for 'append K/V per layer-head'. Fig. 1.2 uses green for Tokenizer and Embedding, orange for Token IDs, blue for Attention, purple for KV Cache. Fig. 1.2's caption explicitly warns 'Color is figure-local decoration ... do not carry a color meaning from Fig 1.1 into this figure', but Figs. 1.1 and 2.1 carry no equivalent disclaimer, and Fig. 2.1's caption nonetheless relies on color.
root_cause: Each figure was styled independently; no book-wide visual-semantics convention was fixed, and the one figure that states a convention (Fig. 1.2) is not the one that depends on it most.
correction: Replace color-only references with shape/label references ('the initialize path', 'the dashed path', 'the path labelled initialize'). Adopt one book-wide palette in which, e.g., KV state is always purple, cache writes always one hue and cache reads always another, and request/control flow always a third; then add the 'color is figure-local' disclaimer to every figure caption that uses color, or drop the disclaimer and make the palette global.
acceptance_test: Every caption that mentions a color also names the element by label; and a reader can classify any colored element in any figure using one book-wide rule.
